title: Permutation in String
keyIdea: A permutation of s1 = a window of s2 with exactly s1's letter counts. Slide a fixed window of length s1.length() over s2, updating 26 counts by one letter out and one letter in, and compare the count arrays.

approaches.name: Sort every window
approaches.idea: For each window of length m in s2, sort it and compare with sorted s1.
approaches.why: n windows, each sorted in O(m log m).

approaches.name: Fixed sliding window of counts
approaches.idea: Count s1 and the first window; then for each step remove s2[i − m], add s2[i], and compare the two 26-count arrays.
approaches.why: Each slide updates two counts in O(1); comparing vectors costs 26.

quiz.q: Why is the window size fixed at s1.length()?
options: A permutation has exactly as many letters as s1

quiz.q: How many counts change when the window slides one step?
options: At most two: one letter leaves, one enters
false: "bo" and "oa" have the wrong letters
